title: feat(lint): note a caller-keyed update policy that declares no check, at info tier
body:
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`@objectstack/lint` 新增一条 info 级规则 `security-update-policy-no-check`:`update` / `all` 行级策略只写 `using`、按 `created_by` 以外的用户列（如 `owner_id`、负责人）匹配当前用户、且没写 `check` 时，给出提示；同时把文档 `access-recipes.mdx` 的示例策略补上 `check`，并加一句组合规则说明。
- 为什么改：没有任何适用策略声明 `check` 时，写入校验由各策略的 `using` 加平台归属兜底（`created_by == current_user.id`）共同组成，作者往往不知道；规则把这条已发布的组合在编写处说出来，并提醒声明 `check` 的副作用。
- 风险与回滚：只是 info，不拒收任何东西，运行时零改动；`os lint --strict` 与 `os validate --strict` 实测都不因它失败（后者按裁决记录 6787890900 已只把 warning 与 error 判为失败）。平台自带权限集里有 23 处会收到这条提示，不影响任何运行。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` 新规则段（`OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_COLUMN` 与紧跟 CBP owner 段之后的循环）;`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` 新条目;`content/docs/permissions/access-recipes.mdx` 第 29–45 行。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-security-posture.test.ts -t "caller-keyed update policy"`，预期 11 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

New rule id `security-update-policy-no-check`, severity **info**, pushed from `validateSecurityPosture` (the existing `AUTHORING_RULES` entry, so it runs on `os lint`, `os validate`, `os build` and the runtime publish gate, never in the gating set).

It reports a permission set's row-level policy when all of these hold:

- `operation` is `update` or `all`, and the policy is not `enabled: false`;
- it declares no `check` (a blank `check` declares nothing, as the runtime reads it);
- its `using` compares a column other than `created_by` with `current_user.id` (`owner_id`, an assignee). The columns are read by the controlled-by-parent owner arm's existing recogniser, `callerIdentityKeyedFields`: either operand order, `record.FIELD`, the SQL bridge spelling, under `&&` / `||`.

The rule it states: a row-level policy with no `check` also admits new rows the ownership floor admits; declare `check` to bound what an update may write. The fix line states the side effect: declaring `check` on any applicable policy takes the USING-only siblings and the floor out of the check, so a creator who is not the owner loses update unless a `check` admits them. It prescribes no way to hand a row back to its creator. `os explain security-update-policy-no-check` carries the composition (ADR-0058 D4; `rls.zod.ts` `check`; plugin-security `writeCheckPolicies`, rule 3).

Each policy is judged as declared. Whether a sibling policy declares `check` for a given caller depends on the sets and positions that caller holds, which the authored metadata does not settle.

The docs recipe in `content/docs/permissions/access-recipes.mdx` now declares `check: 'owner_id == current_user.id'` beside its `using`, and one bullet states the composition and the side effect. Each clause was checked against `packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts` (`check` docblock: the per-operation default, the floor taking part only where the row gate kept it, "only the declared checks decide") and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`writeCheckPolicies`). On an insert the `owner_id` the check reads is stamped by the write middleware before the judged image, so the recipe's own inserts pass it.

Files (7):

- `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`: the id, `OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_COLUMN`, `pushUpdatePolicyNoCheck`, the arm, a header table row.
- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`: the id's `os explain` entry.
- `packages/lint/src/index.ts`: exports `SECURITY_UPDATE_POLICY_NO_CHECK`.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.test.ts`: a new top-level `describe` (11 cases), and the file's meta-guards: the id in `RULE_IDS`, a reachability-corpus fixture, push-site count 21 on `main` to 22, and `check` / `using` on the `policy` read surface (now read by name).
- `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.test.ts`: its whole-table background comparison sets the new id aside on both sides, because the id reads which caller column a policy keys and so differs between `current_user.id` and `current_user.nope`; it reports neither miss that test is about.
- `content/docs/permissions/access-recipes.mdx`: the recipe and the bullet.
- `.changeset/update-policy-no-check-info.md`: patch for `@objectstack/lint`.

New public name: `SECURITY_UPDATE_POLICY_NO_CHECK` from `@objectstack/lint`, which is why `Clause-②` reads `yes (widening)`.

## Tests

`validate-security-posture.test.ts`, new `describe` "a caller-keyed update policy with no check is noted at info tier", each set parsed by `PermissionSetSchema` unless it says otherwise:

1. USING-only `update` on `owner_id`: one `info` finding at `rowLevelSecurity[0].check`.
2. USING-only `all` on `owner_id`: the same.
3. Other caller columns and spellings: an assignee, `record.owner_id`, reversed operands, the SQL `=` spelling, and `created_by` OR-ed with `owner_id`.
4. Control: a policy that declares `check`.
5. Control: a blank `check` declares nothing (reported).
6. Control: a USING keyed on `created_by` only, on one object and on `'*'`.
7. Control: a USING that does not key the caller (`stage == 'prospecting'`, `owner_id in current_user.org_user_ids`).
8. Control: `select`, `insert` and `delete` policies.
9. Control: a disabled policy.
10. Tier: through `runAuthoringRules` for every command the registry serves (`validate`, `build`, `lint`), the finding arrives as `info`, never in the gating set and never as a warning, and the pin asserts that `validate` and `lint` are among those commands. `--strict` counts errors and warnings only on both doors: `os lint` grades an `info` as a suggestion (the CLI's `lint-strict-warnings.e2e.test.ts`), and `os validate` leaves every registry finding of `severity: 'info'` out of its strict count (the CLI's `validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts`, ruling of record 6787890900). On the built CLI, a stack whose only finding is this one exits 0 under `os validate --json --strict` and `os lint --json --strict` (readings under Verification).
11. The message carries the rule sentence, the fix line the side effect, both one line; `explainRule` is defined for the id.

Ablation (one shot, committed first, on head `f7f23a04`; the predicate has not changed since): in the arm, `.filter((f) => f !== OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_COLUMN);` was replaced with `.filter((f) => f === OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_COLUMN);` through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `40364708` to `ebe128c5`). The subject resolves to `src/` through a relative import, so no `dist/` is on the path. The `describe`: 7 failed, 4 passed (the four controls the mutation does not touch). Restored: blob equals HEAD `40364708`, `git diff HEAD` empty; the `describe` then passed 11/11.

## Acceptance notes

- **Census**, run with the built rule over every policy literal (an object literal carrying `operation` and `using`) in `examples/**`, `packages/**`, `content/docs/**`, `skills/**` and `apps/**` (TypeScript AST, static values only, on head `8df583d8`: 1935 files containing "using", 453 policy literals; the 42 not statically evaluable are test fixtures and three runtime builders in plugin-security, `object-membership-keys.ts`, `ownership-floor-alternates.ts` and `platform-ownership-policies.ts`, none an authored permission set). Permission-set hits outside tests: **23**, all in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`: the `_self` policies on `sys_user` (`id == current_user.id`) and on `sys_session`, `sys_two_factor`, `sys_user_preference`, `sys_api_key`, `sys_device_code`, `sys_oauth_consent`, `sys_oauth_application` (`user_id == current_user.id`), at lines 495, 501, 507, 513, 519, 525, 535 (organization admin set), 946, 967, 973, 979, 985, 991, 997, 1007 (`member_default`), 1419, 1431, 1437, 1443, 1449, 1455, 1461, 1467 (external default set). `examples/**`: 0 (the showcase's two policies are `select`). Templates (`packages/create-objectstack/src/templates`): 0, no row-level policies. `skills/**`, `apps/**`: 0. Docs snippets: 0 after this PR; 1 before it, the recipe changed here. No other app's policy is changed in this PR.
- Not judged by this rule: an object's `defaultRowScope`, which has the same policy shape. The census finds 8 of them with this shape, all in `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/` (`sys-api-key`, `sys-device-code`, `sys-oauth-application`, `sys-oauth-consent`, `sys-personal-view`, `sys-session`, `sys-two-factor`, `sys-user-preference`).
- Test fixtures: 26 policy literals in 17 test files have the shape. Only the lint package's own tests read authoring findings over them; the full lint suite passes.

## Verification

Readings name the head they were taken on. `8df583d8` is this branch merged with `origin/main` at `3ec44495` (which carries the `os validate --strict` change), plus the text and pin update.

- Same stack with `check` declared: no finding; exit 0 on all three.

After `pnpm build --concurrency=2` (119 tasks, 83 cached) under the lock it exited 0: 122 published require entry points across 72 packages load. `--ran` on the record: "96 derived, 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
